correctness.rationale: For all odd primes, Guo Lemma 4.1 supplies an exact integer normalized fourth-power expansion. For h<p, the paired binomial product equals (-1)^h modulo p^2 by the product formula. For h>=p, replacing its zero original term introduces p^2 because binom(j+k,k) and at least one central binomial each carry p. Chu-Vandermonde collapses k exactly. For i+j>=p the term has p dividing binom(i+j,i) and another p dividing a central binomial. Guo Lemma 4.2 then reduces the remaining convolution; central binomial squares kill r>(p-1)/2 and r<=half has complete binomial support up to 2r<p. Thus normalized congruence holds in Z[X] modulo p^2 and multiplying by p proves p^3. Published nonstandard identities were read with their proofs; the embedded exact verifier checked identities and all coefficients in bounded cases. Finite checks are explicitly not treated as an all-prime proof.

originality.rationale: The exact matching 2014 source explicitly states the congruence only modulo p^2 as a theorem and names the p^3 target Conjecture 5.2. An alternative Legendre-polynomial draft labels the same question Conjecture 1.5. This proof supplies the missing second-order carry analysis, stronger coefficientwise in Z[X]. Relevant 2025 Delannoy work has a single Delannoy factor, not the fourth power. No covering published record was found in the documented searches. Historical priority remains qualified.

value.rationale: The claim proves a clearly stated 2014 conjecture concerning fourth powers of a natural classical polynomial sequence, rather than a textbook restatement. The coefficientwise Z[X] version is a genuine strengthening for all p-adic arguments. The structural mechanism is a second independent p-adic carry bound at precisely the out-of-range terms that the existing mod-p proof discards; it supplies the missing prime-power degree of accuracy. Explicit conjecture resolution and precise mechanism motivate this exact invariant.
